payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with 0 <= t < 1, floor(n*t) = n-1 if and only if (n-1)/n <= t < 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1 and a real number t with 0 <= t < 1. By the definition of the floor function, floor(n t) = n - 1 if and only if
n - 1 <= n t < n.
Now the right-hand inequality n t < n is automatic from t < 1, since n > 0. Thus, under the standing assumption 0 <= t < 1, the condition floor(n t) = n - 1 is equivalent to just n - 1 <= n t.
Because n > 0, dividing by n preserves the inequality, so n - 1 <= n t is equivalent to (n - 1)/n <= t. Combining this with the given bound t < 1, we obtain
floor(n t) = n - 1 if and only if (n - 1)/n <= t < 1.
This is exactly the claimed equivalence.
result_payload.proof_summary: Use the floor characterization floor(u)=m iff m<=u<m+1 with u=nt and m=n-1. The upper bound nt<n follows automatically from t<1, leaving (n-1)<=nt, i.e. t>=(n-1)/n.
